papers.abstract: $α$-MnTe has emerged as a prototypical altermagnetic material, combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting. Here, we investigate the structural and electronic properties of epitaxial $α$-MnTe layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates. The crystalline and surface quality of the epilayers was characterised by reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), confirming the formation of high-quality, single-phase films. The transport measurements were performed, confirming an antiferromagnetic transition and weak ferromagnetism. The electronic structure was studied using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). At 90 K, both samples exhibit relativistic anisotropic valence band splitting, which is substantially larger along the $Γ$-K direction, reaching approximately 300 meV, than along $Γ$-M, where values of about 150~meV are observed. The magnitude and momentum dependence of the splitting are very similar for $α$-MnTe grown on the two different substrates, indicating the robustness of the altermagnetic electronic structure with respect to the epitaxial environment.

papers.abstract: Interfacing quantum materials with photonic cavity architectures is at the vanguard of materials engineering. The structured electromagnetic fluctuations of a dark cavity environment can renormalize fundamental thermodynamical material properties and energy scales, holding promise to create a rich ecosystem of cavity-induced ground states and functionalities absent in the bare material. However, direct experimental demonstrations that cavity coupling can stabilize or enhance genuinely new phases of matter have remained scarce. In this work, we establish the presence of cavity-induced and cavity-enhanced ferroelectric phases in free-standing SrTiO$_3$ membranes coupled to dark THz-frequency photonic crystal cavities. Using THz spectroscopy, we observe ultrastrong coupling (USC) between the ferroelectric soft mode in SrTiO$_3$ and the cavity resonance. The structural response of SrTiO$_3$ to this USC is measured via second harmonic generation imaging, which reveals a substantial (greater than 400%) enhancement of signal in the cavity environment and a distinct modification of the crystalline symmetry, indicating the onset and enhancement of ferroelectricity. We interpret these observations as resulting from renormalized piezoelectric and flexoelectric couplings, which in turn arise from the cavity-modified dielectric environment. This interpretation is supported with microscopic modeling via DFT-based multi-scale dynamics simulations and by macroscopic Ginzburg-Landau theory. Altogether, our experimental and theoretical results firmly confirm that cavity engineering can indeed be used to create new ground states in materials and enhance existing ones. This work establishes a new paradigm for materials engineering with direct applications for quantum transduction, quantum sensing, and nonlinear integrated photonics.
papers.physics_advance: Coupling a SrTiO3 soft mode to a dark THz cavity is associated with enhanced ferroelectric response and a change in crystalline symmetry, attributed to cavity-modified dielectric, piezoelectric, and flexoelectric couplings.
papers.relevance_reason: The work reports experimental and theoretical evidence for cavity-induced and enhanced ferroelectricity in the quantum paraelectric material SrTiO3.

papers.abstract: We report low-temperature dilatometry and ultrasound measurements on the frustrated quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$ across the entire cascade of field-induced magnetic phase transitions. The whole phase diagram can be recovered from these lattice probes, with distinct anomalies observed at each phase boundary. Elongation along the principal chain axis is found to closely track magnetization throughout the phase diagram. This behavior is interpreted in terms of kinks in the Néel structure and magnons in the transverse-ordered magnetic-BEC phases, each carrying a fixed lattice distortion. A simultaneous analysis of ultrasound and striction data allows us to quantify the strength of magnetoelastic coupling.

papers.abstract: Ferromagnetism and altermagnetism both break time-reversal symmetry, yet their distinct transformation properties under crystalline symmetries forbid direct bilinear coupling between their order parameters. Whether these two magnetic orders can remain thermodynamically distinct while strongly influencing one another remains an open question. Here we demonstrate the homogeneous coexistence of ferromagnetism and altermagnetism in Cr-doped MnTe. By tuning the ferromagnetic ordering temperature across the nearly unchanged Néel temperature with Cr doping, we uncover a striking interplay between the two orders: the ferromagnetic transition becomes a crossover when altermagnetism develops first, whereas the onset of altermagnetism strongly suppresses the out-of-plane ferromagnetic remanence when ferromagnetism develops first. Moreover, spin-orbit coupling enables symmetry-selective interactions through which the ferromagnetic moment controls the altermagnetic domain manifold, with its out-of-plane and in-plane components biasing the time-reversal ($Z_2$) and orientational ($Z_3$) sectors, respectively. Our results reveal how two symmetry-distinct magnetic orders can retain separate ordering tendencies while remaining strongly coupled, providing a route towards internal control of altermagnetic domain states.
papers.physics_advance: Ferromagnetism and altermagnetism coexist in Cr-doped MnTe while retaining distinct ordering tendencies, and spin-orbit-enabled coupling lets the ferromagnetic moment bias altermagnetic domain sectors.
papers.relevance_reason: It reports experimentally evidenced coupled magnetic orders and symmetry-selective domain control in a solid-state magnetic material.

When altermagnetism develops first, the subsequent ferromagnetic transition becomes a crossover; when ferromagnetism develops first, the onset of altermagnetism strongly suppresses the out-of-plane ferromagnetic remanence. The out-of-plane and in-plane ferromagnetic components bias the time-reversal Z₂ and orientational Z₃ sectors, respectively.

papers.abstract: Altermagnetism (AM) is a novel collinear antiferromagnetic phase characterized by spin-polarized bands and zero net magnetization. However, realizing AM in monolayer hexagonal lattices is strongly constrained by lattice symmetry. Here, we propose a mirror-symmetry-based design principle and implementation scheme for realizing AM based on monolayer hexagonal lattices and validate it using holey graphyne (HGY) as a representative system. By examining hydrogenated nonmetal units X$-$H (X = B, C, N, P, and S) introduced along the mirror-symmetry axis and extending the analysis to N$-$F, we identify the configurations that form two antiparallel spin sublattices related by mirror reflection. The N$-$H structure forms a stable altermagnetic ground state, with a momentum-dependent spin splitting up to 148.2 meV. The magnetism originates from $π-π$ superexchange interactions, and H/F functionalization stabilizes intrinsic AM by regulating the local charge distribution. Our work offers insights into the design of light-element altermagnetic materials.

papers.relevance_reason: It predicts a specific altermagnetic ground state in a monolayer material and identifies the symmetry and exchange mechanisms that stabilize it.

papers.summary_en: The authors report direct observation of a light-induced Dirac gap in monolayer graphene under circularly polarized optical driving. They interpret it as a Haldane mass associated with dynamical time-reversal-symmetry breaking and nontrivial Floquet topology.
papers.summary: Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. papers.abstract: Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. While these properties are conventionally determined by the equilibrium Hamiltonian, strong optical fields offer a fundamentally different route by reshaping the Hamiltonian on ultrafast timescales, turning symmetry and topology into dynamically controllable degrees of freedom. Graphene provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing this concept, where circularly polarized light has long been predicted to dynamically break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and open a topologically nontrivial gap at the Dirac point. Despite extensive experimental efforts, direct observation of this Dirac gap-the defining spectroscopic signature of the dynamical TRS-breaking induced topological phase-has remained missing. Here we directly observe this light-induced Dirac gap in monolayer graphene. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the gap emerges simultaneously with the optical field and exclusively under circularly polarized driving, directly linking its opening to dynamical TRS breaking. Together with Floquet theory, we identify the gap with a light-induced Haldane mass and reveal the associated nontrivial Floquet Berry curvature and Chern topology. By demonstrating dynamical TRS breaking in a prototypical non-magnetic material, our results establish optical driving as a route to ultrafast engineering of symmetry and topology, opening opportunities for dynamically tunable quantum matter beyond equilibrium.

papers.relevance_reason: The experiment directly demonstrates a light-induced topological electronic gap in graphene, supported by Floquet analysis linking it to dynamical time-reversal-symmetry breaking.

papers.summary_en: This work uses microscopically parameterized local-moment models to study finite-temperature magnetism in quarter-metal and half-metal phases of rhombohedral graphene, motivated by experiments suggesting fluctuating moments and Pomeranchuk-related order.

papers.abstract: Recent capacitance measurements in bilayer and trilayer rhombohedral graphene reported large magnetic entropy above the Curie temperature, suggesting the formation of fluctuating local moments. Further experimental support comes from scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, which directly visualized honeycomb electron-crystal order that strengthens upon heating before melting, related to the Pomeranchuk effect. Motivated by these experiments, we construct spin-valley local-moment Hamiltonians for the quarter-metal and half-metal phases. We extract their couplings from constrained Hartree-Fock calculations, and solve their finite-temperature thermodynamics with stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo. For the quarter metal we find a continuous 2D-Ising transition at $T_c \approx 0.7$ K, an order of magnitude smaller than the Hartree-Fock estimate (~30 K) and closer to the experimental scale of a few kelvin. For the half metal, we study the field-induced magnetization as a function of temperature with and without proximity-enhanced spin-orbit coupling. When spin-orbit coupling is negligible, intervalley Hund's coupling enhances the magnetic response. Strong spin-orbit coupling, as can be induced by a neighboring transition-metal dichalcogenide, gives rise to the standard spin-canted ground state at zero temperature. Upon heating, the in-plane polarization decreases more rapidly than the out-of-plane polarization. Surprisingly, despite the itinerant nature of the electrons, local-moment models with microscopically determined couplings appear to capture key finite-temperature magnetic properties of rhombohedral graphene without any fitting.

papers.abstract: A local spin fluctuation in the spin-$\tfrac12$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet creates an even number of fractional spinon excitations. We resolve its zero-temperature dynamical structure factor through six spinons directly in the thermodynamic limit. Beyond the established two-spinon contribution of $72.89\%$, the four-spinon response gives approximately $21.90\%$ of the integrated intensity and six spinons contribute a further $4.3\%$, bringing the response to about $99\%$ of both the intensity and first-frequency-moment sum rules. We derive momentum-independent first-moment fractions in the calculated sectors and a general upper-edge law $S_n\sim A_n(k)(ω_{n,u}-ω)^{(n^2-3)/2}$ for every even $n$ at nonzero momentum. The rapid growth of the edge exponent explains why the expanding multiparticle bandwidth carries very little high-energy weight, while higher sectors remain appreciable within the lower-sector continua.

papers.abstract: Moiré superlattices can bind several electrons to each potential minimum, forming few-electron "moiré atoms." Using neural quantum states that obey magnetic periodic boundary conditions, include full Landau-level mixing, and treat both spin sectors, we map the ground state of two-electron moiré atoms in a superlattice as a function of moiré depth and magnetic field strength. At strong field each atom is a spin-triplet maximum-density droplet with canonical angular momentum $\langle L_z\rangle=-1$ and a persistent circulating current: the rotating counterpart of the "Wigner molecular crystal" recently imaged in moiré superlattices. Deepening the wells drives a singlet-triplet transition to non-rotating spin-singlet atoms whose only current is a weak diamagnetic counter-circulation. The transition moves to deeper wells as the field grows, so depth and field together open a window for the formation of rotors. This is the collective analog of the singlet-triplet transition of two-electron quantum dots. At the transition, the orbital magnetic moments of the atoms reverse sign as their spin polarization switches, a joint signature accessible to magnetometry. If the atoms are instead polarized by other means, such as magnetic proximity coupling, the rotors lock at weak field into a spontaneously ordered crystal of dimers in a pinwheel pattern.

papers.abstract: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.

papers.abstract: Altermagnetism has emerged as a new class of magnetism with vanishing magnetization and macroscopic time reversal symmetry breaking. Hexagonal MnTe is a g-wave altermagnet with a 307 K Néel temperature, large spin splitting, and an anomalous Hall effect. However, the relationship between altermagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect in MnTe remains debated. Here, using optical magnetic circular dichroism, we observe hysteresis and a memory effect in a MnTe bulk crystal below 250 K. No hysteresis is seen after polishing the bulk crystal and in thin films. We conclude that the hysteresis in magnetic circular dichroism in the bulk crystal is from surface defects. The similar temperature dependence and a sign change between circular dichroism and the anomalous Hall effect indicate that the origin of the anomalous Hall effect in transport is likely not intrinsic.

papers.abstract: We investigate collective plasma-wave dynamics in a two-dimensional electron fluid subected to a travelling periodic modulation of the effective plasma velocity. Using a hydrodynamic description combined with Floquet-Bloch theory, we show that the travelling modulation acts as a moving plasmonic crystal whose band structure is governed by an effective drift velocity in the comoving frame. We demonstrate that the closure of the Bragg gap at the edge of the Brillouin zone gives rise to an exceptional point and triggers a Krein-type instability through the coupling of positive- and negative-energy modes. Analytical expressions are derived for the instability threshold and growth rate, revealing that self-amplification can occur even when the electron drift remains subsonic in the laboratory frame. Numerical simulations of the nonlinear hydrodynamic equations confirm the theoretical predictions and show the evolution towards a saturated regime dominated by a coherent Floquet-Bloch mode. These results identify travelling plasmonic crystals as a novel platform for wave amplification and non-Hermitian band dynamics in electronic fluids.

papers.abstract: The conventional Bloch quantum geometric tensor (QGT) describes electric-dipole geometry for spatially uniform perturbations and vertical Bloch transitions. We develop a broader framework linking quantum geometry to local and nonlocal electromagnetic response in gauge-field space, placing this tensor within a hierarchy of electric and magnetic multipole quantum geometries. The intrinsic antisymmetric adiabatic response in every electromagnetic channel is a Berry curvature in the space of its conjugate fields. The field-dependent projector uniquely fixes the QGT for that channel, pairing the response curvature with a quantum metric. This construction extends to spatially nonuniform perturbations, whose finite momentum transfer induces nonvertical Bloch transitions. We explicitly construct the current--current QGT connecting Bloch states at $\mathbf{k}\pm\mathbf{q}/2$, providing a unified metric and curvature description of nonlocal current response. In the doubled Brillouin zone, tangential derivatives generate conventional momentum-space QGT multipoles, whereas normal derivatives connect finite-momentum geometry to uniform electric- and magnetic-multipole-pair QGTs. We derive this connection through second order in $\mathbf{q}$. The finite-momentum curvature governs the intrinsic nonlocal Hall response, while an inverse-frequency moment of symmetric optical absorption probes the index-symmetric metric sector.
papers.physics_advance: A current-current quantum geometric tensor at finite momentum unifies nonlocal response with electric- and magnetic-multipole quantum geometries, and its curvature and metric sectors relate to nonlocal Hall response and optical absorption.
papers.relevance_reason: It develops an original theory of Bloch-electron quantum geometry that connects finite-momentum electromagnetic response to measurable nonlocal Hall and optical properties.

papers.authors: Yi-Jian Hu, Yi-Fan Jiang, Wen Huang
papers.summary_en: This study examines whether interband Cooper pairing, without a quantum-geometric contribution, can promote pair-density-wave (PDW) order, using superfluid weight as a diagnostic in two models. It finds that strongly suppressed or negative superfluid weight signals a tendency toward spatially modulated pairing.

papers.abstract: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.
papers.physics_advance: In two models, interband pairing suppresses the superfluid weight without a quantum-geometric contribution; it becomes negative in the examined regimes, indicating an instability toward spatially modulated pairing.
papers.relevance_reason: This theoretical study advances superconductivity physics by identifying interband pairing as a geometry-independent mechanism that can drive a tendency toward pair-density-wave order.
papers.summary_zh: 本文考察不依赖量子几何贡献的带间库珀配对能否促进配对密度波（PDW）序，并以两个模型中的超流权重作为诊断量。研究发现，超流权重显著受抑或变为负值，表明体系倾向于形成空间调制的配对态。
papers.method_en: The authors analyze the Zeeman-split Fulde–Ferrell s-wave superconductor and a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor f-wave pairing. They evaluate the superfluid weight and establish its behavior using analytical and numerical calculations.
papers.method_zh: 作者研究了受塞曼场作用的 Fulde–Ferrell s 波超导体，以及具有最近邻 f 波配对的无自旋蜂窝晶格模型。通过解析和数值计算，他们分析了这两个模型的超流权重。
papers.result_en: In both models, the mean-field superfluid weight has no quantum-geometric contribution, yet it can be strongly suppressed or negative. In the Fulde–Ferrell model, increasing the Zeeman field suppresses the superfluid weight, which becomes markedly negative when extensive gapless excitations, or Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, appear. In the honeycomb f-wave model, the quantum-geometric contribution vanishes and the total superfluid weight is invariably negative. The results support superfluid weight as a qualitative indicator of PDW tendency and provide a microscopic rationale for an interband-pairing-driven instability.
papers.result_zh: 两个模型的平均场超流权重均不含量子几何贡献，但仍可能受到强烈抑制或变为负值。在 Fulde–Ferrell 模型中，增大塞曼场会压低超流权重；当大量无能隙激发（即 Bogoliubov 费米面）出现时，超流权重显著变负。在蜂窝 f 波模型中，量子几何贡献为零，而总超流权重始终为负。这些结果支持将超流权重用作判断 PDW 倾向的定性指标，并为带间配对驱动的不稳定性提供微观解释。
papers.future_en: A natural next step is to test whether the predicted superfluid-weight signatures track PDW formation in systems where interband pairing can be varied, and to assess the diagnostic beyond the two models studied here.
papers.future_zh: 后续可在能够调控带间配对的体系中检验所预测的超流权重特征是否与 PDW 形成相对应，并评估该诊断方法能否推广到本文研究的两个模型之外。

papers.abstract: Magnon polarons, hybrid excitations arising from magnon-phonon coupling, were investigated in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using magneto-Raman scattering measurements at temperatures ranging from 4 K to the vicinity of the Néel temperature ($T_\mathrm{N}$ = 118 K). The lower Zeeman-split component of the magnon-like mode, tuned by the magnetic field toward the lower-energy phonon mode, exhibits an avoided crossing. A model of three coupled bosonic modes shows that the magnon-phonon coupling constant, approximately 2.7 cm$^{-1}$ at low temperatures, decreases significantly with increasing temperature, following a trend similar to the temperature-induced softening of the magnon mode. This decrease in magnon-phonon coupling is discussed in terms of a possible reduction in sublattice magnetization due to thermal fluctuations.

papers.abstract: We investigate triplon topology and the thermal Hall transport in a columnar valence-bond solid of a spin-$1/2$ honeycomb-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet. Inequivalent triangular sublattices, modeled by $J_2^A\neq J_2^B$, remove inversion symmetry at nearest-neighbor bond centers and allow in-plane Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interactions. We identify the two symmetry-allowed in-plane DM vector patterns and present detailed results for the pattern parallel to the bonds including an out-of-plane magnetic field. Within a harmonic bond-operator treatment, we determine the triplon bands, their Berry curvatures and Chern numbers, and the triplon thermal Hall conductivity. The DM interaction and magnetic field generate nonzero Berry curvatures, but the numerically integrated Chern number of every isolated triplon band vanishes. Nevertheless, the energy-dependent Bose weighting of positive and negative Berry-curvature regions produces a finite thermal Hall response at nonzero low temperatures. We delimit the dilute-triplon regime in which the harmonic transport calculation is expected to be reliable. These results show that a vanishing Chern number band does not directly constrain the triplon response of a valence-bond solid. We also comment on the effects on the columnar valence-bond solid phase of a DM interaction between next-nearest-neighbor spins characterized by an out-of-plane vector pattern.
papers.physics_advance: In the modeled valence-bond solid, DM interactions and a magnetic field yield finite triplon thermal Hall conductivity even though every isolated triplon band has zero Chern number.
papers.relevance_reason: This is an original theoretical study of triplon topology and thermal transport in a quantum antiferromagnet.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究含面内 Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya 相互作用的蜂窝晶格自旋 1/2 J1–J2 反铁磁体柱状价键固体中的三重态激发拓扑及热霍尔输运。尽管每条孤立三重态激发能带的陈数均为零，模型仍呈现有限的低温热霍尔响应。
papers.method_en: The authors use a harmonic bond-operator treatment for a columnar valence-bond solid with inequivalent triangular sublattices, focusing on the DM pattern parallel to nearest-neighbor bonds and including an out-of-plane magnetic field. They calculate triplon bands, Berry curvatures, Chern numbers, and thermal Hall conductivity, and delimit the dilute-triplon regime for the harmonic calculation.
papers.method_zh: 作者采用谐波键算符方法研究三角子晶格不等价的柱状价键固体，重点分析平行于最近邻键的 DM 矢量排列，并纳入面外磁场。他们计算三重态激发能带、Berry 曲率、陈数和热霍尔电导，并界定谐波计算适用的稀薄三重态激发区域。
papers.result_en: The inequivalent triangular sublattices remove inversion symmetry at nearest-neighbor bond centers and permit in-plane DM interactions. The DM interaction and out-of-plane field generate nonzero triplon Berry curvature, although the numerically integrated Chern number of every isolated band vanishes. A finite thermal Hall response nevertheless arises at nonzero low temperatures because Bose weighting distinguishes positive- and negative-curvature regions in energy. The results show that a vanishing band Chern number does not by itself constrain the thermal Hall response of a valence-bond solid.
papers.result_zh: 不等价的三角子晶格破坏最近邻键中心处的反演对称性，从而允许面内 DM 相互作用。DM 相互作用与面外磁场会产生非零的三重态激发 Berry 曲率，但数值积分所得每条孤立能带的陈数均为零。由于玻色权重对不同能量处的正、负 Berry 曲率区域赋予不同权重，体系在非零低温下仍具有有限热霍尔响应。结果表明，能带陈数为零本身并不能限制价键固体的热霍尔响应。
papers.future_en: Further work could test the predicted thermal Hall response within the identified dilute-triplon regime and assess how the discussed next-nearest-neighbor DM interaction affects the columnar valence-bond solid.
papers.future_zh: 后续研究可在本文界定的稀薄三重态激发区域内检验所预测的热霍尔响应，并考察文中讨论的次近邻 DM 相互作用如何影响柱状价键固体。
papers.tier_reason_en: The paper provides a model-specific theoretical analysis of triplon bands and thermal transport, including a useful distinction between Chern number and thermal Hall response, but the abstract does not indicate a broader experimental or conceptual advance beyond this setting.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 本文针对特定模型分析三重态激发能带与热输运，并阐明陈数和热霍尔响应之间的重要区别；但摘要未显示超出该体系范围的更广泛实验或概念性进展。

papers.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
papers.announcement_time_basis: arXiv dated batch and official 20:00 Eastern release schedule
papers.authors: Yuxin Duan, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Song Luo, Long Zhang, Zhanghai Chen
papers.summary_en: This study realizes electrically tunable dipolar exciton polarons in a van der Waals homobilayer, using interlayer excitons with spatially separated charges as dipolar impurities. It reports stronger interactions than for conventional intralayer exciton polarons and shows that Fermi-sea layer polarization controls their many-body dressing.

papers.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.
papers.physics_advance: Dipolar exciton polarons in a van der Waals homobilayer have binding energies over four times those of conventional intralayer polarons, while Fermi-sea layer polarization controls hybridization and orientation-selective many-body dressing.
papers.relevance_reason: The experiments establish controllable many-body exciton-polaron physics in a low-dimensional quantum material and identify how dipole orientation and Fermi-sea polarization shape it.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在范德华同质双层中实现了电学可调的偶极激子极化子，其中电荷空间分离的层间激子充当偶极杂质。其相互作用强于传统层内激子极化子，并显示费米海的层极化能够调控其多体缀饰。
papers.method_en: The authors use an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer to realize interlayer excitons with permanent electric dipole moments coupled to a Fermi sea. They examine the exciton–electron interactions and compare the resulting polaron behavior for different Fermi-sea layer polarizations.
papers.method_zh: 作者利用电学可调的范德华同质双层，实现具有永久电偶极矩并与费米海耦合的层间激子。研究考察激子—电子相互作用，并比较不同费米海层极化条件下的极化子行为。
papers.result_en: The dipolar exciton polarons have binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. A Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to one layer suppresses this hybridization and yields orientation-selective many-body dressing. The results establish dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization as joint controls of the interactions. The authors identify the platform as a route toward electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.
papers.result_zh: 偶极激子极化子的束缚能超过传统层内激子极化子的四倍。费米海会诱导取向相反的偶极极化子发生杂化；将费米海限制在单层则会抑制这种杂化，并产生取向选择性的多体缀饰。结果表明，偶极取向和费米海层极化共同决定相互作用。作者指出，该平台有望实现电学可调相互作用，并探索由偶极极化子介导的巡游电子间吸引。
papers.future_en: The abstract identifies electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons as opportunities enabled by this platform. Further experiments could examine these proposed regimes; the abstract does not claim that such electron attraction has already been observed.
papers.future_zh: 摘要指出，该平台为电学可调相互作用以及偶极极化子介导的巡游电子间吸引提供了可能途径。后续实验可研究这些设想的物理状态；摘要并未声称已经观测到这种电子吸引。
papers.tier_reason_en: The work establishes a new, electrically tunable polaron platform and reports a greater-than-fourfold binding-energy enhancement alongside controllable hybridization and dressing. These are strong, quantitative results for a focused condensed-matter study, supporting PRL-level significance without enough evidence in the abstract for a broader top-tier claim.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 该工作建立了新的电学可调极化子平台，并报告了超过四倍的束缚能增强，以及可控的杂化与多体缀饰。这些是凝聚态物理专题研究中的有力定量结果，足以支持 PRL 水平判断，但摘要证据不足以支持更广泛的顶级期刊评估。
